club_details.playing_style: Possession-based, with quick switches of play to the wingers and full backs who push high.
club_details.crest: A navy shield with an amber street lamp at its centre and a harbour chain across the bottom. Four small chimneys above the shield recall the Harrow Quay lamp factory, and a ribbon below carries the motto 'Lux in Portu' (light in the harbour).

chairman.bio: Owner of a local ferry and shipping company and a Foundry End season-ticket holder for forty years. In 2015 he led the supporters' trust that bought the club back from outside owners, and he has chaired it ever since.

history: Brackwater Athletic was founded in 1889 by workers of the Harrow Quay lamp factory, who played on a cinder pitch next to the docks. The club took its nickname, The Lamplighters, from the factory's night shift, who lit the street lamps on the way to evening matches.

The club turned professional in 1904 and won its first league title in 1932. Its golden era came between 1978 and 1986, with three league titles and two Meridian Cups under head coach Walter Penhallow, whose statue stands outside the North stand.

In 2004 the club left its historic ground at Cinder Lane and moved to the Lanternworks Stadium, built on the site of the old lamp factory. The academy, opened the same year, has produced more than forty first-team players.
After a difficult decade, Brackwater finished third last season, their best league finish since 2002.

records.biggest_win: 9-0 against Dunstrow Athletic in the Meridian Cup, January 1958.

legends.fact: Led the club to three league titles; the statue outside the North stand shows him holding his famous flat cap.
Scored 187 goals for the club, a record that still stands.
Played 512 league games, more than anyone in club history, and kept goal in the 2001/02 title season.

traditions: Before kick-off the North stand holds up thousands of small amber lights, a nod to the lamp factory.
The club anthem, 'Light the Quay', is sung as the teams walk out.
A lamp is lit in the club museum after every home win and stays on until the next match.

head_coach.tactical_style: An attacking 4-2-3-1: patient build-up through the two holding midfielders, then quick switches to the wingers. The full backs push high, the number 10 has a free role, and the team presses straight after losing the ball.
career: Played 280 games in midfield for Brackwater Athletic Women (1997-2012) and captained them for six seasons.
Coached the Brackwater under-21 side (2014-2018), then was assistant coach at Kingsfold Rovers (2018-2021).
Head coach of Vanbridge United from 2021/22 to 2023/24, winning the Meridian Championship in 2023/24.
Head coach of Brackwater Athletic since the summer of 2024; third in the Meridian League in 2025/26.

chairman.bio: Runs a ceramics firm founded in the town's kiln district and has chaired the club since 2019. She paid for the restoration of the two brick kilns behind the South terrace, now the club museum.

history: Calderholm United was formed in 1894 by merging two works teams from the town's pottery kilns, which is why fans still call the players The Kilnmen.
The club won its first league title in 1952 and added three more, the last in 2015/16, when a squad built on a ferocious press lost only two games all season.
Its ground, The Kilnyard, keeps two of the original brick kilns behind the South terrace, now used as the club museum.
Calderholm finished fifth last season, Dario Castellane's third in charge.

records.biggest_win: 8-1 against Copperhythe FC in the Meridian League, during the 1967/68 title season.
records.most_appearances: Fergal Mulvane, 498 games in all competitions (1988-2003).

legends.fact: Saved the club from bankruptcy in 1949 by selling her pottery business.
Captained the 1997 title team and never received a red card.
Scored the goal that won the 2016 title, a header in the 93rd minute, and is the club's record scorer.

traditions: Away fans travel to Brackwater on 'the derby boat', the old estuary ferry.

head_coach.tactical_style: A direct 4-4-2 built on a high press: the two strikers press the centre backs, the wide midfielders deliver early crosses, and the team is drilled to win the ball back within six seconds of losing it.
career: Played as a central defender in the Italian lower divisions until 2005.
Coached in the Italian lower divisions for fourteen seasons (2009-2023), with two promotions.
Head coach of Calderholm United since the summer of 2023; fifth in the Meridian League in 2025/26.

stadiums.name: Lanternworks Stadium
stadiums.roof: covers every seat; the pitch is open
stadiums.history: Built on the site of the Harrow Quay lamp factory where the club was founded. The four red-brick chimneys of the factory were kept and stand behind the North stand; at night they are lit amber.
notable_matches: August 2004: the opening match, a 2-2 draw with Calderholm United in the Estuary Derby.
August 2018: Brackwater beat Ravensgate City 2-1 to win the Meridian Super Shield, the first trophy lifted at the Lanternworks.
2019/20: the record attendance of 60,388, for the derby against Calderholm United.
May 2022: the stadium hosted the Meridian Cup final, won by Hollin Vale United.

head_to_head.name: The Estuary Derby
head_to_head.story: Brackwater and Calderholm face each other across the Calder estuary, less than nine kilometres apart. The first meeting, in 1896, was abandoned at half-time when the tide flooded the pitch. Since then the derby has been played 212 times in all competitions, and the old ferry that links the two towns is still known as 'the derby boat'.

last_meeting.summary: In the last meeting, in the 2025/26 Meridian League, Brackwater Athletic and Calderholm United drew 0-0 at the Lanternworks Stadium.

programme.item: The Lamplighters Store opens at the foot of the Main Stand (sector W1).
Two under-12 academy sides play a short exhibition game on the pitch.
Lumo, the club mascot (a lamplighter with a lantern and a long brass pole), greets families in the Lamplighters Stand and poses for photos at the Family Desk.
Club legend Desmond Ockley walks a lap of the pitch carrying the derby lantern, which is handed to the home captain before kick-off.
The amber light display starts in the Foundry End and spreads around the stadium.
The teams walk out to the club anthem, 'Light the Quay', sung by the whole stadium.
Handshakes, team photos and the coin toss.
Half-time (around this time): the academy under-14 side does a lap of honour after winning its regional tournament.
